test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 12 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Consider the following statements about the force acting on a current-carrying straight conductor placed in a magnetic field:

(a) The direction of the force remains the same even when the direction of magnetic field is reversed.

(b) The direction of the force can be determined using Fleming's left-hand rule.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only (b).**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The thumb points in the direction of the force experienced by the conductor**, the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field, and the middle finger points in the direction of the electric current, according to **Fleming's Left Hand Rule.**
 
• This arrangement of the thumb, forefinger, and middle finger of the left hand is perpendicular to each other.
 
• **A current-carrying straight conductor receives a force perpendicular to the direction of the current flow **and the field when it is put **in an external magnetic field.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Fleming’s Right Hand Thumb Rule:

 
• This rule is frequently applied as a mnemonic to help remember the way the three axes—X, Y, and Z—orient on a three-dimensional plane.
 
• It says that when we position our right hand's thumb, forefinger, and middle finger perpendicular to one another, then:
 
 
• The thumb indicates the direction in which the conductor is moving in relation to the magnetic field.
 
• The direction of the magnetic field is shown by the forefinger.
 
• The middle finger is pointing in the induced current's direction.
